newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil cancels SWATH deal with Smedvig.
newsitem.headline: Statoil cancels SWATH deal with Smedvig.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap ASA (Statoil) said on Wednesday it had cancelled a contract with Smedvig ASA for the construction of the so-called SWATH specialist vessel.
Statoil spokeswoman Nina Steihaug said the company would probably instead use its existing rig fleet in cooperation with Transocean Offshore ASA and other companies.
"We suspended the Smedvig contract at the end of July," she said. "The news now is that we have cancelled the contract."

"We will probably use normal rigs instead for Aasgard under the contract with Transocean or other offshore companies. We may rearrange the rig contract with Transocean, our largest rig contractor," she said.

Smedvig in May signed a letter of intent for a one billion crown service contract with Statoil on the Aasgard development off mid-Norway and other future projects. It would use a new vessel comprising the small waterplane area twin hull (SWATH) concept.
"When we realised that the original SWATH concept was not able to qualify technically, we wanted to rethink and so we suspended the contract," Steihaug said.
"Now we have looked into the matter and so far nobody has come with a technically viable SWATH concept. It was an idea that did not come through."
She said the Aasgard development would not be affected by the cancellation.
